items.title: The US ISM Services report was particularly strong, both overall and relative to expectations, with nearly all activity and price subcomponents rising robustly (employment being the lone exception). Notably, overall business activity expanded to a six-month high, new orders climbed to their highest level in over three years, and prices paid reached a four-year peak. #economy #markets

items.title: In line with the consensus forecast, annual Eurozone inflation rose from 2.9% in July to 3.3% in August, its highest level since September 2023. While core and services inflation were more contained—both falling somewhat—this headline print solidifies market expectations of an interest rate hike when the ECB’s Governing Council meets next week. #economy #markets #europe #inflation #eurozone #ECB @ecb

items.title: Good morning. With oil prices higher, government bond yields are on the move again around the world. One of the most notable moves is in the UK—what I have characterized here and elsewhere as one of the “high beta” advanced economies—where the 10-year has traded up to a level not seen in almost 20 years (Bloomberg data below), while the 30-year yield is at a level not seen in almost 30 years. #economy #markets #bonds #yields #oil

items.title: Here’s the link to FSB (Financial Stability Board) Chair Andrew Bailey’s letter to the G-20 warning that “markets remain vulnerable to a potentially disorderly correction that could spread across borders, particularly given fragilities in sovereign debt markets, vulnerabilities in private credit, as well as stretched asset valuations.” Think of it as another illustration of the inherent promise/peril innovation equation: what makes the considerable upside possible (and needs to be unleashed) comes with downside risks (that need to be identified and mitigated).  #economy #markets #ai
